tom: Kicking off canary for search-service v3.2.0 now — 5% traffic, change window 14:00-15:00 PT. Watch p95 latency and error-rate. Thresholds: errors > 2% or p95 > 400ms -> backout.

deploy-bot: [deploy-job 7890] Canary start OK. Instances: 2/10. Artifact: build/sha-abc123. CI: https://ci.internal/7890

sasha: @tom noted. Pre-approved backout runbook = search-backout-v2 (internal link). Key steps: pin traffic, trigger rollback job, validate no DB schema revert required. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/search-backout-v2

elaine: If we need to pin, here are the commands — run in ops shell:

```
# pin traffic to previous stable
rctl pin service/search 3.1.9 --reason "backout canary 3.2.0"
# trigger automated rollback
deploy-bot rollback job=7890
```

liam: Quick Q: any DB migrations in v3.2.0? If yes we need a migration-safe backout path.

sasha: No schema changes — just feature-flag toggles in this build. Backout is safe for DB. I'll still run smoke tests after pin.

ops-bot: ALERT: Canary error-rate threshold breached (2.4%) at 14:08 PT. Metric: search-queries/errors = 2.4% (window=1m). :warning:

tom: Ack. Initiating backout now. @sasha please run the pin command, @liam start the rollback verification smoke tests, and @elaine coordinate support notifications.

sasha: Done — pinned to 3.1.9 and triggered rollback. Pin log id=9987. Command output: "pin applied, routing updated". Rolling canary down.

deploy-bot: [deploy-job 7890] Rollback completed -> now serving v3.1.9 across canary nodes. Canary drain complete. Duration: 3m.

elaine: Support notified, status page updated to "degraded -> recovered". Created follow-up ticket: ENG-4521 (postmortem + validate canary test corpus).

liam: Smoke tests passing on pinned traffic. No data drift observed. Good to close the window early if no other signals.

ops-bot: NOTE: Runbook checklist items marked: pin_applied, rollback_triggered, smoke_tests_ok. All steps green.

tom: Thanks team — closing thread. Action items: attach logs to ENG-4521 and review canary test thresholds. :thumbsup:
